# `prefer-testing-expect-equal`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: quick fix · Options: none

Reports `std.testing.expect(actual == literal)`-style assertions.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

`expectEqual` reports expected and actual values, producing a substantially more
useful test failure.

## When it fires

It applies when one side is a simple literal and the other one postfix
expression on one line (a name, field, length, call, index, dereference or
unwrap chain such as `list.items.len`, `record.count` or `count()`), so the
argument order of `expectEqual(literal, actual)` is established safely. A
comparison inside a larger condition is left alone, and `null`, `true` and
`false` count only against a plain name: `expect(std.mem.find(...) == null)`
tests absence, and `expect(f() == false)` reads better as `expect(!f())`.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

test "sum" {
    const n: u32 = 2;
    try std.testing.expect(n == 2);
}
```
